lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush’s ecstatic welcome shows how much Elizabeth’s dog matters to their plans.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert admits shortening visits just to take her hand, an early private tenderness.

lines.text: May your father indeed be able to love me a little, for my father will never love me again.
lines.note: Elizabeth’s fear that her father will never love her again frames the cost of leaving.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Flush’s loss becomes a shared crisis and the start of their dog-stealer saga.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Their Flush-and-banditti comparison captures the playful logic running through the letters.

lines.text: To be parted from you so long, teaches me the necessity of your presence—I am your very, very own.
lines.note: Separation teaches Elizabeth the necessity of Robert’s presence.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush returns and lies on the sofa, turning the dog-stealer saga into domestic relief.

lines.text: What a glorious dream; through nearly two years—without a single interval of blankness,—much less, bitter waking!
lines.note: Robert calls their two-year courtship a glorious dream without a single blank interval.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth yields her will to Robert’s as the elopement plan closes.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Robert says words can never tell how perfectly dear she is to him.

lines.text: And all in the midst, the bells began to ring.
lines.note: Church bells during the wedding day mark the moment they can no longer hide.

lines.text: I did hate so, to have to take off the ring!
lines.note: Elizabeth hates taking off the ring and asks Robert to put it on again.

lines.text: And forgive the inveterate jesting, which jests with eyes full of tears.
lines.note: Elizabeth’s jesting with eyes full of tears balances fear and love.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s farewell line that by tomorrow she will have only Robert to love her.
